messages:
Maya Patel: evening — heads up, nightly eval picked up a sharp increase in short-answer truncation on the new v6b weights (brought up yesterday). failing ~12% of the prompt-set where we used to be ~1%.
Liam O'Connor: ouch. any examples?
Maya Patel: yeah, here's one from the 'FAQ-compact' prompt set: expected: 'You can reset by going to Settings > Account', got: 'You can reset by going to Settings >' and then it stops. another: expected: 'Contact support at support@example.com', got 'Contact support at' then repeated token.
Arjun Rao: do we see any consistent token boundary? looks like mid-word cut or end-of-sentence?
Maya Patel: mostly ends right after a special-char or after token id 50256-ish. sometimes repeats last token twice.
Cassie: @Maya can you paste the raw generation with token ids?
Maya Patel: paste below — trimmed:
```
prompt: "How do I reset my password?"
model: redwood/v6b-2026-03-19
gen: "You can reset by going to Settings >"
token_ids: [1012, 3021, 4054, 50256]
logprobs: [-0.2, -0.4, -0.6, -3.2]
```
Liam O'Connor: logprob crash at last token is telling — maybe EOS mispred or tokenizer mapping changed. did tokenizer metadata change in this build?
Arjun Rao: I checked the model package — the tokenizer file is identical hash to v6b-candidate we used last week. weights diff was nontrivial though (merge from opt-finetune branch).
Maya Patel: eval-bot shows this only on quantized runners (int8-ggml path) — CPU hosted evals are fine. Dedicated GPU runs also fine.
infra-bot: noticed: deploy redwood/v6b-2026-03-19 -> gpu-pool-2 completed 2026-03-19T22:14:02Z
Arjun Rao: interesting. so quantization path + new weights -> failure. could be KV cache alignment or packing artifact.
Cassie: do we have reproducer on local quant runner? if yes, let's run with verbose tokenization.
Maya Patel: repro attached to the eval ticket (link). ran local ggml quant 8-bit with --verbose-tokens, output shows tokenizer emitting an extra <unk> token id 50256 at sequence end for these prompts.
Liam O'Connor: 50256 is our sentinel unknown/EOS mapping in that tokenizer variant. If quant path is misreading the sentinel mapping due to byte-order or padding, it could chop generation.
Arjun Rao: also saw repeated last token in some traces — could be loop in sampling when EOS id is ambiguous. check sampling policy code for equality vs is.
Cassie: quick test idea: run the tokenizer on the prompt + expected continuation and compare tokenization across python-fasttokenizer vs ggml tokenizer. differences?
Maya Patel: did that — python-tokenizer -> tokens end with 3452, 1123, 0 (EOS=0). ggml-quantized runtime -> ends with 3452, 1123, 50256. so they disagree on EOS id.
Liam O'Connor: maybe tokenizer vocab.json had two special tokens remapped when we merged newer merges. The runtime expects eos_id=0 but quant runtime uses fallback eos_id=50256.
Arjun Rao: if the runtime doesn't consult the model's config for special ids (bug in packaging script maybe), it will use default eos. check model-card and bundled tokenizer.json in the deployment tarball.
Maya Patel: looked at the tarball — tokenizer.json lists "eos_token_id": 0. but ggml header in the quant artifact has eos=50256 (printed during load). so mismatch between runtime header and tokenizer.json.
Cassie: that explains truncation. why only in quant path? probably the quant conversion script wrote the wrong header value. the GPU path uses huggingface loader which reads tokenizer.json at runtime. ggml uses its own header.
Liam O'Connor: action items: (1) rollback quant artifact for v6b on hosted quant runners; (2) investigate quant conversion script defaulting eos to 50256 when certain metadata missing; (3) add a quick assert in runtime to check tokenizer.json eos_id == artifact header eos_id and fail-safe log.
Arjun Rao: I'll take (2) and the assert. Cassie can you coordinate rollback? Maya can you collect a small failing prompt set and attach to the rollback ticket so we can regression-test?
Cassie: will coordinate rollback now. pinging infra to drain quant pool and redeploy previous artifact. :white_check_mark:
infra-bot: starting rollback: deploying redwood/v6b-2026-03-12-quant -> quant-pool-1; estimated 3min.
Maya Patel: attaching prompt list to ticket. also noticed quantized GEMM round-offs slightly changed final logits — worth running diff post-rollback to ensure no other drift.
Liam O'Connor: yes run the nightly eval quick-run on both artifacts and produce delta CSV. if only eos mismatch, diff should be limited to truncation cases.
Arjun Rao: implementing a CI check: quant-converter will now embed tokenizer header into the ggml file and we will assert-on-load. also adding unit test where eos is nonzero.
Cassie: rollback complete. quant-pool-1 now on v6b-2026-03-12-quant. infra-bot: all instances healthy.
Maya Patel: re-run of nightly subset on quant runners shows failure rate back to baseline 0.9%. good catch everyone.
Liam O'Connor: nice. follow-up: record in the onboarding checklist that quant conversion must preserve special token ids and include a checksum.
Maya Patel: opened PR with checklist updates and linked converter patch.
Arjun Rao: PR for converter in review. will add logging to alert if header/tokenizer mismatch >0.
Cassie: thanks all. closing the triage thread, marking eval ticket resolved after further monitoring. :thumbsup:
